utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of them. We had situations like this daily, so, yes, I was kept abreast.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, I see that these documents were also sent to Mr. Bajro Pizovic, the commander of the Bregava Brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now let's see what it is that Mr. Pizovic answered, what his response was to the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, about this document, P1913 that you're aware of and familiar with, we can see the situation, when an ABiH soldier wears an insignia, he can be arrested and detained for 15 days, but what happens on the 16th day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 16th day, he would be released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And did you come across such instances when you arrested an ABiH soldier who was detained for 15 days and released on the 16th day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember precisely, but I think that they were released in accordance with what is said here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Pavlovic, in the municipality of Stolac or in the territory of your battalions, was any member of the Army of BiH arrested because they wore a BiH Army insignia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, not because they wore those insignia, but if they did not respect the rules, that is, if they -- if he was on leave, he would have to carry a document about him being on leave to be allowed to stay in our zone, and if he didn't have such a document, he would be arrested.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If there are no further questions about this, let us look at the next document, 4D473. In the final part of item 2, could you please interpret this? So the commander of Bregava answers to the commander of the 1st HVO Brigade about the warnings about entering the zone of responsibility without announcement, and now I quote: "This is well known to you, that a large number of Muslim soldiers are in your formations, and they are Muslims and belong to this people, so it would not be good if the defined organisation formation of your units would be disrupted." Can you explain what this means? And if you knew about this at the time, how did you feel about it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: It follows clearly from this that the commander of the Bregava Brigade at any given moment can deploy a part of Muslim soldiers who are part of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us now try to sum up what these documents state. We have seen from these documents that in April 1993, some people were taken prisoner, so I want to ask you, based on these documents, what would you say who these arrested people were?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: They were members of units that did not execute their tasks, but engaged in arbitrary actions in their zones of responsibility and outside the zones, and they were members of the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In accordance with your knowledge, Mr. Pavlovic, in April 1993, in your territory, was anybody arrested who was not a member of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information that in April 1993, in the territory of the Stolac municipality, that anybody was in -- house arrest?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No way, that was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, have you ever heard of the Begovina facility in the Stolac municipality?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was that facility near the front-line or in the center of Stolac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: That facility was at the very -- was at the first line. Bunkers were 50 metres removed, if at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, these bunkers, when were they built?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Right after liberating Stolac from the Serbian aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That means in mid-1992; right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in June.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some documents now, and after that we'll try to draw some conclusions from them. The first document is 4D33 - yes, that's it - and that's a document of the 42nd Mountain Brigade of the Army of BiH. Tell us, Mr. Pavlovic, is that the Bregava Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can tell by the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. In the third-but-last item, it reads that all Muslim members of the HVO should be called upon to side with their own people. The next document is 4D34. Again, the security organ of the 42nd Mountain Brigade two days later. It also says that: "Co-operation must be established with our fighters in the HVO, and the seriousness of the situation must be pointed out to them." The third document is 4D35. In the final part of the document, that is, item 3, it is said that the morale organ for IPD and religious issues should draft an information plan for the Muslims in HVO units in the municipalities of Capljina and Stolac. It is signed by Bajro Pizovic on the 18th of April, 1993. The fourth document is 4D36. It's a document of Arif Pasalic, the commander of the 4th Corps of the Army of BiH, dated May the 2nd, 1993. In item 3, second paragraph, it reads that: "We linked up with our people and the HVO, and the --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please show us where she's reading from?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not listening to the interpreters, so I thank the colleagues who warned me. So we described the document, and I'm saying that in item 3, second paragraph, Arif Pasalic is saying that: "Linking up with our men in the HVO was carried out." Then he goes on to state that men from the Capljina HVO have the task of taking the village of Tasovcici and the bridge in Capljina. And then other tasks are listed, such as seising the town of Stolac with "our people in the HVO," et cetera. I don't have to read the entire document. We've seen it here a number of times. The fifth document about the same topic is 2D300. In these official minutes, the document is in Croatian, and item 2 states that pressure is being exerted on Muslims in the units --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise to my colleague for interrupting. I don't want to object, but, Your Honour, I just wish to note that thus far we've shown documents and -- 4D34, 35, and 36 to the witness without a single question being asked, so I wonder if that's an appropriate way of going -- proceeding. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I announced that. In this series of documents, we are dealing with documents that are exhibits already, so the witness doesn't have to comment on every one, and I did say that I would ask my question after a series of documents, this document being the last in that series. So let me just outline the content. So it is stated that pressure is being exerted on all Muslims who are in HVO and MUP units to leave those structures, and if they don't, they are threatened by physical liquidation or by burning their homes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, based on these documents, I have a question for you, Mr. Pavlovic. At that time, did you know about the policy of the ABiH to link up with Muslims in the HVO and that it was planning to initiate some actions in co-operation with them?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What was the source of your information?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, the most reliable source of information were our soldiers in the HVO and the police, on whom pressure was being exerted, and they complained to us because they didn't want to leave our units. And the other sources were other intelligence sources; that is, intercepted conversations, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Pavlovic, did that information cause you to change your attitude toward your soldiers of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, there is no reason for me to change my attitude towards someone who came to me to complain because he wanted to stay in my unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether any special measures of any kind were taken toward your soldiers of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No measures -- no special measures were taken, except once we had learned which HVO members had initiated these events, we would have deployed that unit differently or we would strengthen the share or step up the share of Croatian soldiers and the like. Those were the measures that we took.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let us now take a look at another document, but we should move into private session because the document is protected, I'm being told.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at document P10258. It's a letter sent by Alija Izetbegovic to Franjo Tudjman. The date is handwritten and says "22 May 1993." And Alija Izetbegovic says here: "It has come to my attention from numerous sources that yesterday," which means on the 21st of May, "an intensive ethnic cleansing of Muslim people started yesterday in Stolac upon Boban's order." Did you know about this letter, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I learned about this letter from President Boban.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the following document, 4D2000. Mr. Pavlovic, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you give this document to the Defence of General Petkovic during the proofing?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Mate Boban ask you to explain what was going on at Stolac as a consequence of which Alija Izetbegovic complained of ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the president asked me to provide information about the events at Stolac. Am I to describe it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, if you can, but very briefly.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I received a phone call from his office, and they put me through to the president. And he asked me, What kind of problems are there at Stolac? And I, as I knew that there were no problems at the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think the president is Boban here, the president referred to, right, just to make sure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know what exactly you mean, because the first letter shown was Alija Izetbegovic's letter to Franjo Tudjman, and this is Boban's letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: In the meantime, the witness has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I received a phone call from his office, put me through to the president. He asked me, angrily, what kind of problems there were at Stolac, and I replied that there were no problems at all, and that was really how it was. And we had a short conversation, and I think I was able to convince him. And he asked me whether I could leave my command post, and I said, Why not? There are no problems. And he demanded me to submit a report about the events at Stolac and come and see him if I could. And I knew what it was about. I had been informed orally that it was about refugees and the expulsion of civilians. And I linked up with Mr. Markovic, the president of the HVO, and we drafted a document which corresponded to the facts. We took it to Mr. Boban together and showed it to him, and then the president showed me this document, the letter sent by Mr. Izetbegovic to Mr. Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, I'm going to put a question to you about that. Are you able, in this courtroom now, under oath as they often say, can you tell us whether in Stolac, during those months, except for capturing members of the Bregava Brigade, were there any other arrests, expulsions, or crimes against Muslims, or anything that could considered an element of ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, not at all. Nothing like that occurred.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. Now we're going to move to our next topic, which will probably interest our Judges, too. This is Topic 36, the 30th of June, 1993, when a drastic change in the relationship between Muslims and Croats occurred. For a start, Mr. Pavlovic, can you please tell us if you know what happened on the 30th of June, 1993, in your Operations Zone South-Eastern Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Something tragic happened which I am unable to understand even now, and that is that co-fighters which had been together at positions for months attacked their colleagues from the back, disarmed them, killed them, captured them, and together with Bosnia and Herzegovina Army in the Bijelo Polje area, expelled the Croatian civilian population from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you say "co-fighters," who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I'm thinking of the soldiers of the HVO of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you specify the area where this happened, what you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: This happened in the northern part of the Mostar municipality, so it was north of Mostar, some 25 to 30 kilometres north of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. When you tried to compare this event, as it had been described to you, to some other incident that happened during the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, what would you say? Is there any event that would compare to it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know or I didn't hear that anything like that happened outside of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the history of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: General Praljak, when he testified in this courtroom and described this event, said that after that, total war between Croats and Muslims started in that part of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in the area of this operations zone. Would you agree with such a qualification by General Praljak or would you have a different comment or provide a different assessment of the incident?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with that, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, according to what you know, can you please tell us what the percentage of Muslim soldiers was in HVO units in the area of this operations zone, South-Eastern Herzegovina? You can talk about your units.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: As far as my units are concerned, I can give you almost precise information, and I think the situation was similar in other units. I had at least 50 per cent of Muslims in my units, at least 50 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us what would have happened had the Muslim soldiers in your units behaved the way the HVO Muslim units behaved in the Mostar area, that they betrayed their Croat comrades and betrayed -- and joined the HVO, what would have happened to the lines of defence of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: I'm going to object to the question, Your Honour, that that calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you permit me to explain. Had we had a civilian here, I would absolutely agree with my learned friend, and there would be no need to agree, actually, because I would not have put that question at all, but we have a commander of the HVO and we're asking him to evaluate the security reasons for the implementation of a certain measure. I believe the question is quite appropriate, because I believe at that moment the witness should have made the assessment whether Muslim soldiers presented a danger for his units or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, put your question, but use it only as far as military consequences are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, I'm putting this question to you as a military commander who, after this betrayal by Muslim HVO soldiers very close to your operations zone, had a large percentage of Muslims in your units, and that your Muslim soldiers, had they done what the Muslim soldiers of the HVO did in the area north of Mostar, what would have happened with your lines of defence?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Our lines of defence would have been under threat, and I think that they would have had to be abandoned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you say "abandoned," what does that mean? Can you be very specific, please? Would the HVO still be able to hold these lines or not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, it would not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And what would that have meant at that point in time for the Serbian Army, which had its positions not that far from yours?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: That would mean that they could have walked into the town with a very small number of forces and could have captured the whole area around Stolac and broader.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to your estimate as a military commander, would such a situation have presented a security issue, a security problem?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And as a military commander, can you tell us that in such a situation, did you think that you had to take some measures in order to prevent you from losing control over the lines of defence that you were in charge of?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, something had to be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Can we now see what it was, exactly, that you tried to do? I just have an additional question, and I thank you -- for being reminded. We're talking about the dangers facing Stolac because of a possible betrayal by Muslim soldiers in your units, and when we recall that order by Arif Pasalic from the 2nd of May, 1993, that we looked at earlier and which mentioned, as one of the tasks, "capture Stolac in co-operation with our people in the HVO," when we link those two situations together, how would you, as a military commander in charge of the defence of Stolac -- would you say that there was a danger facing Stolac or not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Stolac was facing quite a considerable danger, meaning that if there was an internal conflict, the enemy could capture Stolac without major difficulty whenever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at document P3019. This is an order by the Main Staff of the HVO. I'm correcting the number. It's P3019, 3019. Yes, that is correct. It's an order by the chief of the HVO Main Staff, General Petkovic, of the 30th of June, 1993. I'm going to say this. We will go back to that part. It's an order on the disarmament and isolation of HVO soldiers of Muslim ethnicity. We can look at page 2 of this document. The order was sent to the Operations Zone of South-East Herzegovina. Let us look at the parties that the order was forwarded to. Mr. Pavlovic, can you please tell us who else received this order within the operations zone?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: It was sent to the commanders of the 2nd and 3rd HVO Brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, which brigade did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I was in the 1st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And what did we say? Who was the commander of that 1st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Nedjeljko Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we conclude that the commander of the operations zone did not send this order to the 1st Brigade, I will ask you whether this order -- this order did reach you in some way, as a person who was in one of the companies or the forward command posts of an HVO brigade?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, elements of this order did reach me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I am asking you this: This order, in the form of this document, did that reach you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: First we're going to analyse this document, and then we're going to try to see how you received the order on the disarmament. Can you please look at item 10 of this document. And in item 10, it says: "A close co-operation and activity co-ordination should be established with all forces in your zone." And then in brackets it says: "(Anti-terrorist groups, the police, and the military police outside your structure)." Can you please explain, Mr. Pavlovic, whether we can conclude, on the basis of this, that the disarmament action would be implemented with the co-operation of four groups of units; first of all, the units of the HVO which were part of the operations zone, then the anti-terrorist groups, then the police, and then the military police? Would you interpret this paragraph 10 in that way?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you please speak up a little bit and repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, Mr. Pavlovic, was the chief of the Main Staff authorised to command civilian police?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you be a little bit louder, please?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No. Okay, I need to come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to your information, was the -- did the chief of the Main Staff have the authority to command the military police?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you help us now, Mr. Pavlovic, to understand this: If units of the HVO under the command of the chief of the Main Staff participate in one action and some armed units not under the command of the chief of the Main Staff also participate in that action, who at that point in time in Herceg-Bosna was the person who would be able to decide about a joint action by all of these armed formations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If you allow, Ms. Alaburic, I would like to complete the series of questions that you had begun before and ask the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: order troops to give orders to brigades, to operations zones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I thought that was understood, because this was an order to the operations zone. So, Judge, based on your knowledge of the situation in Herzegovina, we have the situation where in one action we have military units participating under the command of the chief of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm going to repeat my question. If, in one action, we have military units under the command of the chief of the Main Staff participating, and if we also have armed formations who cannot receive commands from the chief of the Main Staff because they're not in his chain of command, who at that point in time is the person in Herceg-Bosna who can issue an order for such a joint command to be carried out in the first place?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Such an order can be issued by the supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Now let's try and analyse item 8 of this order. Item 8 states as follows: "In units where there are still Muslim soldiers, they should be disarmed and isolated." Now, to the best of your understanding, Mr. Pavlovic, the word "isolate," did that mean "arrest" or did it mean some other measure?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: The word "isolate," as I understood it then and now, means that you have a certain group which you have to disarm and escort them to an area in which that group will be secure, where that group will not be able to operate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now look at the next excerpt, where it says: "In places with Muslim inhabitants within an area of responsibility, all military-capable men should be isolated." Now, in your understanding of this sentence, does it mean that the Muslim conscripts should be isolated in places where they are located or whether something else should be done?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: This can be interpreted in two ways. In the places in which they lived, they could not have been isolated.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, for reasons of their security, because those places were close to the front-line, to begin with, and there was the danger at all times from that, from the enemy artillery fire. And in the second case, if we were to isolate people in those places, there could be an attempt at an attack with the other groups that we mentioned, and then they could fall casualty in that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, the sentence goes on to state that: "Women and children should be left in their houses or apartments." So tell us now, did the order reach you, too, whereby the civilian population should be left alone, unprotected?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we move into private session for a moment, because I'm going to show a protected document and quote the statement made by a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm still looking at this document. Before we move into private session, I have a question on document P3019. Colonel, I listened to the questions very carefully, and I also listened to your answers, but at the same time I was looking at this document which we know very well. We've already seen it. I'll tell you why I'm surprised. This document dates June 30th, 1993. It's an important date, but there's no stamp saying "Urgent," and it is not encoded. This document is sent to the commander of the south-eastern zone, Mr. Miljenko Lasic. All he's going to do is inform the 2nd and the 3rd Brigade of the HVO of the content of this document. And when we look at the order, what do we note? Items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 seem to be very technical. There was a request for reinforcement of lines, there was reference to the trigonometric points and so far and so on. But in item 8, the crucial question is addressed, the disarmament of Muslim soldiers, and I really wonder why this has to be placed in item 8, whereas it seems that this was an urgent and necessary measure. Why is it sort of lost within technical -- other technical items? Do you have any idea? What's your take on it? Do you have any explanation for this? Of course, when Mr. Petkovic will come and testify, I will ask him the same question, because he signed this order, but this is only a few weeks from now. And you're here, so I might as well put the question to you also.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, General Petkovic would be best placed to give an answer to that question. However, my answer would be this: I think that at this point in time, the essential thing was to establish the defence lines because the forces were continuing to attack, enemy forces continued to attack. So what was important here was to reinforce the lines, fortify them, strengthen them, and protect oneself from further attack, and all the other activities that one needs to undertake would come subsequently. Now, in reading this order from items 1 to item 10, all this lasts for just a few minutes, and the commander receiving this order will be able to read through it and then decide what to do. It is possible that for one unit, the prime task would be to set up a defence line, and that unit was one that had already suffered an attack, but on the other hand, for another commander who had still not come under attack in that same zone, item number 8 might be the most important task in hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps this is a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let's have a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed. You have 35 minutes left, based on our calculations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May we move into private session, as I had requested, because we're going to deal with a protected document, a document under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Witness, did you know about these speculations in the HVO brigade?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: There might have been speculations, but I can't confirm who issued the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now let's see what was happening in your area. Now, from whom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Alaburic. I find that answer a bit -- very meager: "There may have been speculations ..." Can you specify what you meant, what you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I -- as I understood, judging by the statement made by this witness, that he meant specifically the person mentioned, that that gentleman had issued the order, which I can't confirm because I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. But I don't know whether that was actually the gist of the question, whether it was Mr. Markovic who had issued the order or whether there were discussions about the order itself. I was of the opinion that you were, Ms. Alaburic, referring to the contents of the order. And if the witness only -- if you only have doubts about whether it was Mr. Markovic or not who issued the order, then does that mean that you have not heard about any reactions to that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I know who issued me the order. Now, guess-work and speculation is another matter. Anybody can say anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Colonel. Generally speaking, among soldiers, indeed, we know that there were sometimes Croats and Muslims side by side in those units facing a common enemy, the Serbs. Generally, there is a sort of military feeling of solidarity among soldiers who experience things together. On the 30th of June, the soldiers learned that they had to disarm their brothers-in-arms, i.e., the Muslims here in this case. As far as you knew, were there any discussions on this issue among soldiers, or did they all find it totally normal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I understood your question, you were asking whether there were discussion and debates among the soldiers. Once the soldiers had been given their assignment, that is to say, to disarm the unit, they didn't have time to talk to anybody about it, to discuss it, because it happened in a very short space of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Mr. Pavlovic, who did you receive the order from telling you to disarm the Muslim soldiers in Stolac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I received orders from my brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nedjeljko Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, was it a written or oral order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: It was an oral order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: How were you given this order, where and when?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: The oral order was given to me at Domanovici, the command post of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: On what day? When was that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: In the evening of -- I think it was the 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you meet with Commander Obradovic alone or were there some more people there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I think there was a short briefing at Commander Obradovic's.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: At the meeting, did you discuss the situation in Bijelo Polje and the surrounding parts north of Eastern Mostar, after the treachery of the Muslim HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My commander informed me about the situation. He informed all of us, in fact, of the situation, and issued us our tasks, although at that time the soldiers didn't know much about this because there wasn't much information going 'round.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, at that meeting did you and the military commanders conclude that this event and the danger of new treachery on the part of the Muslim soldiers represented a security risk or was this considered to be a fairly benign event?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at all events, once we learnt what had happened, when we learnt the whole truth of it, then we were able to make our conclusions, and we expected that this might happen in our unit, too, imminently.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you go back to Stolac after the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And did you have a meeting with any of your associates?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Not that evening, but on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Who did you meet?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: That evening, if you will allow me to tell you, we raised our combat readiness, and the next day I had a meeting with my battalion commanders. With the commanders of the 4th and 5th Battalions, in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us what the first reaction was of those Stolac soldiers [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the first reactions were -- well, you know what it's like when you get such a sensitive assignment. People didn't believe what was going on, they didn't know what was going on, so they were in a quandary. However, once I explained the situation to them and what might happen in their very own unit, and what the intentions of the enemy was in the near future, then they saw that the order had to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to correct the transcript. In line 20, it says "Stolac soldiers." I said "Stolac battalions." We're referring to the two battalions, the HVO and the other one in Stolac. Now, Mr. Pavlovic, I am interested in the immediate reaction of the commanders before you explained to them what the situation was. When you said that they professed disbelief, could you explain to Their Honours what their initial -- what the initial reaction of your commanders was?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the first reaction was -- of the commanders was that they were unable to understand that a person they had spent a year with up at the front-line, that they now had to disarm that person and send him away. Now, later on I heard from them that this happened at a lower level to them later on, so they wondered whether anything could be done to avoid total disarmament of these individuals.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Pavlovic, if I understand you correctly, the HVO Croatian soldiers were not happy to have to undertaken action against their Muslim colleagues; is that right? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is right, and there were some very touching scenes in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. And after that, you explained to your brigade commander -- battalion commanders what the reasons for that were, and what was their conclusion afterwards? Did they feel that it was justified that these measures that had been ordered were taken or not? What was their position?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when we analysed the situation, they were in full agreement with the order that was received and they undertook to implement the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you said that the meeting took place on the following day, we're talking about the 1st of July, 1993, are we?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And tell us, how was the action of disarming the Muslim HVO soldiers organised in your area?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, we received reinforcements. Those were two companies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let me immediately ask you from whom you got those reinforcements.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: From the brigade command. So those were two companies, and then we made a plan of how those two companies should be used.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Before that, tell us where those companies that came to help you out came from.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: One was from our brigade and the other from the Ljubuski Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The one from your brigade, from which town was it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: From Neum.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do continue now, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: So we drafted a plan. We distributed the positions among us. We sent platoons there from those companies, and locals, police officers, took them to those positions. They reported to the commanders of the units that were currently holding the positions. In co-operation with those commanders -- or, rather, those commanders explained to their soldiers what had happened, and that they must surrender their weapons, and that they must leave the positions temporarily, and the newly-arrived soldiers took the places of the soldiers of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did the soldiers of Muslim ethnicity surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were no incidents in that respect. They knew what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And what did you do with those Muslim HVO soldiers who surrendered their weapons at their positions?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: We used the same means of transportation that -- with which we had brought the new soldiers. We took the Muslim soldiers to the factory at Stolac, and then they were taken to Grabovina in Capljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you say "Grabovina," was that an HVO barracks at Capljina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did those HVO soldiers of Muslim ethnicity spend the night in the factory at Stolac or were they further transported to Capljina on the same day?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know of anyone having spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Who told you that the disarmed HVO soldiers should be transported to the Capljina barracks?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I have already said that those people could not remain in the territory of Stolac because one enemy shell would have been enough to harm many of them, so I asked the brigade command to give us a facility where these people can be isolated, and they decided that they should be taken to Capljina barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Once these Muslim HVO soldiers were taken to Capljina, did you have any subsequent contacts with those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, now think back a few days before that event. Were there any indications that anyone at Stolac, Capljina, Mostar, or any other place known to you was planning any kind of actions to arrest or isolate a larger number of Muslims? Was anything of this kind being prepared in any part of Herceg-Bosna known to you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No. The moment we received the order that we have to do that, I think, was the most difficult moment of my life, and it was very hard for me to execute that order, because if you spend a year with someone at the front-line, it is very difficult to isolate these people. Even today, I live with some of them, and I have no problems with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us now, Mr. Pavlovic, as you spoke about these things after the war, too, and you read memoirs and other literature, and you probably have other sources of information, too, do you know any circumstance that you could mention here to these honourable Judges that anybody in the HVO, before this time in 1993, could have been considering to implement such a wide-scale action of isolating Muslim HVO soldiers or other people of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, I've never heard anything of that kind, not even jokingly said. We had good relations, and there was really no need for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for these explanations. Now, please, let's try and see, in some documents, what was happening to your brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, Ms. Alaburic has asked you a series of interesting questions, because they made it possible to understand how amazed you were and what kind of problems, from the point of view of your conscience, you had after the Muslim soldiers were disarmed in the afternoon of the 30th of June. My problem is as follows: We saw a document a moment ago, P3185. This is an order by the investigative judge, Dragan Budimir, for Arif Pasalic to be arrested, and also for members of the Bregava Brigade to be arrested. Looking at this document, I discover that the investigative judge, who wants to have all these people, 10 people in all, arrested, had been seized by the regional military prosecutor of Mostar of the issue on the 16th of June, on the 16th of June, 1993. So there was at least somebody who, 15 days before the 30th of June, knew that there was a danger, and that was the military prosecutor. So how can you explain that the prosecutor, the military prosecutor, was aware that there was a problem, whilst you, two weeks later, you only discover there is a problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I can tell from this document, and to the extent I understand it, I believe that this is exclusively about members of the ABiH, nobody else, because the persons listed in this document are members of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but this is a document about the ABiH members, but that was because there was a plan by the ABiH against the HV. And the document you saw before, 4D36, it's an internal document, internal to the 4th Corps, dated 2nd of May, 1993. That document shows that there was a plan for the taking of Stolac by the Muslim HVO members. It's written black on white. So they knew that there was a danger, but you, as the commander of your unit, you didn't perceive there was such danger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, I mentioned a short while ago that we were aware of that threat, but we had taken a series of measures and activities to prevent that from happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, if I remember correctly, you spoke about measures of trying to control and the reorganisation of some units because of the information that there were plans of the ABiH in connection with Muslim members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We would strengthen the units that we considered exposed to such a threat.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What you were now explaining was in a situation when there was information about the existence of such plans, but another situation was when the HVO had lost control over some territory due to also the treachery of some Muslim soldiers, and that would be a significant difference, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If you can, tell us, briefly, the action of isolation was also applied to conscripts of Muslim ethnicity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you explain how you treated conscripts? What were they to you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Conscripts were treated as the reserve force of an army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were conscripts of Muslim ethnicity, to your mind, a reserve force of the BiH Army?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now see what happened to your brigade when it was left without a significant number of soldiers of Muslim ethnicity, who had been isolated. Tell us, in absolute numbers, how many soldiers of Muslim ethnicity were there in your two battalions?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: About 600, perhaps slightly over that number.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And in the 1st HVO Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I have no accurate data, but maybe up to 2.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Taking into consideration the composition of those who were isolated, do you know how many of them were HVO soldiers and how many others of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: I really have no accurate data, but I believe that in the territory of Stolac municipality, numbers were equal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So we're talking about a 50:50 ratio?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at P3149. It's an order signed by the chief of the Defence Department and chief of the HVO General Staff of the 3rd of July. It's the Knez Domagoj Brigade. Was that your brigade?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was the brigade really restructured in accordance with this order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the following document, P3151. In this order, under 1, we see that the commander of the 1st Brigade is trying to identify the Muslims who can remain in the units because they are considered loyal, but I am now interested in item 2(b), which says that the Forward Command Post Stolac is being abolished. Was it this order that abolished your establishment position?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, Mr. Pavlovic, does an HVO soldier lose his status, that of a soldier, namely, if he is locked up for some breach of discipline or any other reason?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: No, the status is not lost.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, when can an HVO soldier lose his status of a soldier?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC
utterances.text: He can lose his status if the unit is demobilised, that is, when he is no longer needed, or if he leaves the unit without leave, if he goes AWOL. And I don't know of a third way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask to go into private session again, because I will be referring to documents and I would like to protect the privacy of the persons involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session. Witness, please take a look at the map on the screen. Can you confirm that you were very familiar at the time with Mostar and its surroundings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can confirm that I did know Mostar and its environs quite well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You're very familiar with Mostar and its surroundings. Please look at point 2 on the map. It's close to Rastani. Did you know Rastani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rastani, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This map is a little bit difficult to read, but we saw other maps. We know that there is a road along the river that flows by Rastani, and we know because we've already had a witness who told us about this. We know that Rastani at one point in time was occupied by the HVO in August 1993. Through questions being put by the Prosecutor at the time, we found out that this road was under HVO fire, and because of that there could be a problem with traffic. Now, you know -- you're very familiar with this place, so can you tell us whether the Muslims in East Mostar could use another road or other trails in order to avoid being under HVO fire because of the HVO positions in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This map is quite small, so it's not really possible to see a lot on it. But based on what I know, instead of Vrapcici, which is the neighbouring settlement - it's a place which is on the way out of Mostar - can be reached by a road from a part of the town called Zalik, and this M-17 road at that time was exposed to fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You are saying that the M-17 was under fire or was exposed to fire. Very well. But was there another road that would not have been under HVO fire that could have been used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just said, Your Honour, that I think that there was a road from the Zalik neighbourhood towards Vrapcic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You confirm this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the other road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were around -- could you tell us exactly when you were around Mostar, from which months to which months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the environs of Mostar -- actually, I was in Mostar, itself, from March 1992 until the 1st of July, 1992, and from the 27th -- and from the 20th of July, 1993, until early -- actually, until mid-1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were in Mostar from July 20th, 1993, until mid-1994. As far as you remember - and this is an important question - as far as you remember, did the Muslims who lived in East Mostar -- as of July 20th, 1993, until mid-1994, could these Muslims living in East Mostar, could they leave East Mostar, with much precaution, of course, could they leave East Mostar without being under HVO fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think -- actually, I'm convinced that they could leave without being under direct HVO fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you know, are there any Muslims from East Mostar who were able to leave this part of the city of their own volition and without getting killed on the road taking them to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were able to go to Jablanica of their own volition, without being hurt or hit on the road, because there was a road -- an open road from Mostar to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just before we call it a day, because we have a few minutes left: When you answered Ms. Alaburic earlier, you said in passing that the 4th Corps and the VRS were undertaking trade, selling small weapons and some food over the line that was dividing them, and you seemed to be quite sure of yourself when you said that. So as far as you know, do you know whether any Muslims from East Mostar actually left East Mostar by being able to go through the lines held by the VRS maybe because VRS officers had been bribed, were corrupt, or because they just paid their way through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't there, myself, so I really cannot be sure or say that there were such cases. But the information that reached me, the intelligence information that reached me, does confirm that. We even have information -- or had information at the time that a meeting was held at corps level, at the top level. Very often, we would find an unexploded shell that was of Serbian manufacture, and recent manufacture, at that, and there were also many other pieces of intelligence indicating to us that such contacts were actually taking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last question, and then we will stop for today. As far as you know, did Serbian artillery shell Mostar, either West Mostar or East Mostar? Are you aware of any such incidents where the VRS artillery would shell either the HVO in West Mostar or the ABiH in East Mostar? This is a question that encompasses all sides.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have information that they did fire shells at our positions that were guided by members of the B and H Army, but I cannot really claim something like that decisively here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're telling us at some times the VRS was shooting [as interpreted] Mostar West, but these were shots that were guided by members of the BH Army. Had you learned this -- have you learned this from prisoners of the ABiH, or from intelligence sources, or just by rumours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have that information from intelligence sources, provided to us by our intelligence people who were in charge of -- or who were tasked with monitoring these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's 7.00 p.m. We will resume with the other Defence counsel tomorrow. We're sitting in the afternoon this week. Witness, please come back for the hearing, which will start at 2.15. And I warn you, once again, please do not contact anyone until tomorrow. Thank you, and see you tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 17th day of November, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
